# thoth_policy (Resource)

Manages a policy rule in one environment (dev or prod). A rule written with an API key, which is how Terraform writes, always waits for a person: a new rule starts pending, and a change to what a live rule matches or does puts it back to pending, out of enforcement, until a signed-in org admin approves it. status shows that.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "thoth_policy" "hold_deletes" {
  environment = "dev"
  name        = "Hold deletes"
  type        = "scope"
  enforcement = "review"
  applied_to  = ["all"]

  # Hold every call to these tools for a person's approval.
  rules_json = jsonencode({
    tool_names = ["orders.delete", "customers.delete"]
  })
}
```

A rule lives in one environment. Changing `environment` replaces it; to move a dev rule to
prod, promote it with the configuration preview (`preview_policy_rule`) or the API. A promotion
always starts a `pending` prod copy, and with `replace_existing` over a prod rule that is live,
that rule keeps enforcing its old content until a person approves the replacement.

## Rules wait for a person

Terraform writes with an API key, and what a key writes never applies until a signed-in person
approves it:

- A new rule starts `pending`, with an org admin's key too. Thoth does not enforce a pending rule.
- A change to what a live rule matches or does (any field but `enabled`) puts it back to
  `pending`. **The rule is out of enforcement from that apply until a signed-in org admin, with
  MFA, decides it.** The new content applies only once approved; the old content does not keep
  running.
- `enabled` is true for every rule that is not disabled, so a pending rule shows no difference in
  `terraform plan`, and the gap is invisible from the plan alone. The provider warns when it reads
  a pending or rejected rule, and the computed `status` attribute shows it.
- An org admin's key cannot approve its own change either. Where the audited self-approval
  bypass is on, an admin key that re-enables a rule its owner wrote is refused with 403
  (`policy_rule_bypass_needs_person`): the bypass is used only by a signed-in person with a
  verified factor, never by a key. Terraform never approves a rule.

To see and resolve pending rules, outside Terraform:

- List them: the dashboard (Settings, Governance), `thothctl governance policies list`, or the MCP
  configuration server. Look for `status` `pending`.
- Approve or reject one as a signed-in org admin: the dashboard, `thothctl governance policies
  decide`, or `preview_policy_rule` with action `decide` over MCP (confirmed in the browser with MFA).
  The approver must be a different person from whoever changed the rule, unless the org's audited
  self-approval bypass is on. A rejected rule is never enforced; change it to send it back for
  approval.

Plan changes to live rules for a time when a person can approve them straight afterwards, and
check `status` after an apply.

`enabled = false` turns a rule off. Turning it back on is allowed for content a different person
approved.

Import with `environment/policy_id`:

```shell
terraform import thoth_policy.hold_deletes dev/6ae1441907c1c31e7e44ca5a
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `enforcement` (String) monitor, review or block.
- `environment` (String) dev or prod. Changing it replaces the rule; promote a dev rule with the configuration preview or the API.
- `name` (String) Rule name.
- `type` (String) scope, budget, risk or data_access.

### Optional

- `applied_to` (List of String) Agent IDs the rule applies to, or ["all"] (the default).
- `argument_conditions` (Attributes List) Numeric checks on the call's arguments, all of which must hold, together with the tool match in rules_json (tool or tool_names). At most 5. A review or block rule fails closed: a call that leaves the argument out matches (set when_missing to "no_match" to opt out), and a value that is present but not a plain number, or a key that differs from the argument only in case or separators (Amount for amount), holds the call for review. The rule depends on the exact argument name; synonyms such as amt are not recognised. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--argument_conditions))
- `description` (String) Rule description.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the rule applies once it is approved. It is true for every rule that is not disabled, a pending one included, so a rule waiting for approval shows no difference in a plan: read status. A pending rule stays pending until a signed-in org admin approves it, and an API key cannot approve its own change or turn on a rule its owner wrote (403).
- `rules_json` (String) What the rule matches, as a JSON object (for example with jsonencode()) with one of tool, tool_names, model_name, model_provider, purpose, data_classification, min_token_count or min_estimated_cost_usd, or the overlay keys blocked_tools and allowed_tools. A rule with none of these is refused, because Thoth would never apply it.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation timestamp.
- `id` (String) Resource ID: environment/policy_id.
- `policy_id` (String) Policy rule ID assigned by Thoth.
- `status` (String) pending, active, disabled or rejected. pending means Thoth is not enforcing the rule (or, for a change to a live rule, its new content) until a signed-in org admin approves it; the provider warns when it reads one.
- `tenant_id` (String) Tenant ID from provider configuration.
- `updated_at` (String) Last update timestamp.

<a id="nestedatt--argument_conditions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `argument_conditions`

Required:

- `argument` (String) An argument name or a dotted path of at most 4 names (expense.amount). Names are letters, digits, _ and -, starting with a letter. Case matters.
- `operator` (String) gt, gte, lt, lte or eq.
- `value` (Number) The number to compare against: finite, between -1e15 and 1e15.

Optional:

- `when_missing` (String) match or no_match: whether a call that leaves this argument out matches. Unset, a review or block rule matches it (fail closed). A present value that is not a plain number holds the call for review whatever this says.
